questions.question: A car runs for one hour with a speed 60 km per hour, for 2 hours with a speed 70 km per hour and for 5 hours with a speed 50 km per hour. What is the average speed of the car in km per hour?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Total Distance = (60 × 1) + (70 × 2) + (50 × 5) = 60 + 140 + 250 = 450 km

Total Time = 1 + 2 + 5 = 8 hours

Average Speed = 450 ÷ 8 = 56.25 km/h

**∴ The correct answer is 56.25 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed for 1st part = 60 km/h, Time = 1 hour

Speed for 2nd part = 70 km/h, Time = 2 hours

Speed for 3rd part = 50 km/h, Time = 5 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

When the numbers 8651, 8018 and 7807 were divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case was the same. The value of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When given numbers leave the same remainder when divided by the greatest number x, then x is the HCF of their absolute differences.

Calculate the differences: (8651 − 8018) = 633, (8018 − 7807) = 211, and (8651 − 7807) = 844.

x = HCF of (633, 211, 844).

Since 211 × 3 = 633 and 211 × 4 = 844, the HCF is exactly 211.

**∴ The correct answer is 211.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Three numbers: 8651, 8018, and 7807.

When divided by the greatest number x, the remainder is the same in each case.

**Formula Used:**

If numbers a, b, and c leave the same remainder when divided by the greatest number x, then:

x = HCF of (|a − b|, |b − c|, |c − a|)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 8651, b = 8018, and c = 7807.

⇒ Difference 1 = |a − b| = |8651 − 8018| = 633

⇒ Difference 2 = |b − c| = |8018 − 7807| = 211

⇒ Difference 3 = |c − a| = |7807 − 8651| = 844

⇒ Now, we need to find the Highest Common Factor (HCF) of 633, 211, and 844.

⇒ Factors of 211 = 211 × 1

⇒ Factors of 633 = 211 × 3

⇒ Factors of 844 = 211 × 4

⇒ The greatest common factor for all three differences is 211.

**∴ The correct answer is 211.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF for Same Remainder

When a given set of numbers leaves the exact same remainder when divided by a common highest number N, then N is the HCF of the absolute differences between pairs of the given numbers.

HCF for Given Different Remainders

When numbers a, b, c leave specific remainders p, q, r respectively when divided by the greatest number N, then N is the HCF of (a − p), (b − q), and (c − r).

LCM Concept for Remainders

The smallest number which when divided by a, b, c leaves the same remainder R in each case is found using: LCM(a, b, c) + R.
</p

questions.question: The ratio between the original price of a movie ticket and increased price of the movie ticket is 10 : 13. What is the increase in the revenue of the cinema hall, if the original price of the movie ticket was ₹250 and total 3600 tickets were sold as per the maximum capacity of the cinema hall that is 3600 persons?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of original to new ticket price = 10 : 13.

Price increase per ticket = 13 − 10 = 3 units.

Since 10 units = ₹250 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹25 ⇒ 3 units = ₹75.

Total revenue increase = Increase per ticket × Total tickets sold.

Revenue increase = ₹75 × 3600 = ₹2,70,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,70,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original price of a movie ticket = ₹250

Ratio of original price to increased price = 10 : 13

Total number of tickets sold = 3600

 
 Original Price: 10 units = ₹250
 
 10 units = ₹250
 
 +3 units
 
• 
 

 ₹75 Increase
 Total Revenue Increase = 3600 tickets × ₹75
 = ₹2,70,000

**Formula Used:**

Total Revenue = Price per ticket × Number of tickets sold

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original price be 10x and increased price be 13x.

⇒ Given, 10x = 250 ⇒ x = 25

⇒ Increased price = 13 × 25 = ₹325

⇒ Original Revenue = 250 × 3600 = ₹9,00,000

⇒ New Revenue = 325 × 3600 = ₹11,70,000

⇒ Increase in revenue = 11,70,000 − 9,00,000 = ₹2,70,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,70,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Revenue Formula

Revenue = Price per item × Quantity sold. Any percentage or proportional change in price or quantity directly impacts the overall revenue.

Percentage Change in Revenue

If price changes by a% and quantity changes by b%, the net percentage change in revenue is given by: (a + b + ab/100)%.

Ratio and Proportion Application

If two quantities are in the ratio a : b and the first quantity is known to be x, then 1 unit equals x/a. The second quantity or any difference can be calculated directly by multiplying units with x/a.

questions.question: When the numbers 7807, 8022 and 8667 were divided by the greatest number x, then the remainder in each case was the same. The sum of the digits of x is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the differences between the given numbers: 8022 − 7807 = 215 and 8667 − 8022 = 645.

The greatest number x leaving the same remainder is the HCF of these differences.

x = HCF(215, 645) = 215.

Sum of the digits of x = 2 + 1 + 5 = 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 7807, 8022, and 8667.

**Formula Used:**

Greatest number dividing a, b, and c leaving the same remainder = HCF of |a − b|, |b − c|, and |c − a|.

**Calculations:**

⇒ First difference = |7807 − 8022| = 215

⇒ Second difference = |8022 − 8667| = 645

⇒ Third difference = |8667 − 7807| = 860

⇒ Now, find the HCF of 215, 645, and 860.

⇒ 215 = 215 × 1

⇒ 645 = 215 × 3

⇒ 860 = 215 × 4

⇒ HCF of (215, 645, 860) = 215

⇒ The greatest number x = 215

⇒ Sum of the digits of x = 2 + 1 + 5 = 8

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF Rule for Same Remainder (Value Not Given)

Greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving same remainder = HCF of (|a − b|, |b − c|, |c − a|).

HCF Rule for Different Remainders

Greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving remainders p, q, r = HCF of (a − p, b − q, c − r).

HCF Rule for Same Given Remainder

Greatest number dividing a, b, c leaving same given remainder R = HCF of (a − R, b − R, c − R).
</p

questions.question: Two cyclists, M and N, start from the same point on a 1500 m circular track, cycling in opposite directions. M cycles at 18 km/hr and N at 22 km/hr. How long (in seconds) will it take for them to meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 18 + 22 = 40 km/hr = 40 × (5/18) = 100/9 m/s.

Time taken to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed.

Time = 1500 ÷ (100/9) = 1500 × 9 ÷ 100 = 135 seconds.

**∴ The correct answer is 135 seconds.**

questions.question: The average age of 26 students of a class is 43 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 44 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the net deviation method for averages:

Age of new member = Old average + (Total members × Increase in average)

Age of teacher = 43 + (27 × 1)

Age of teacher = 43 + 27 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 26

Average age of students = 43 years

New average age (including teacher) = 44 years

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

 
 26 Students (Avg: 43)
 +
 
 Teacher
 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 27 Members (New Avg: 44)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 26 students = 26 × 43

⇒ Total age of 26 students = 1118 years

⇒ Total number of people after including the teacher = 26 + 1 = 27

⇒ Total age of 27 people = 27 × 44

⇒ Total age of 27 people = 1188 years

⇒ Age of the teacher = Total age of 27 people − Total age of 26 students

⇒ Age of the teacher = 1188 − 1118 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ having n₁ and n₂ elements respectively are mixed, the new average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Excluding a Member

If a member leaves a group, the value of the excluded member is Old Average − (Remaining Members × Decrease in Average).

Replacement in Average

When one person is replaced by another, the age of the new person = Age of removed person + (Total members × Change in Average).
</p

questions.question: Rodney sold 153 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 63 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP for 153 chairs = 153 units.

Gain obtained = SP of 63 chairs = 63 units.

Cost Price (CP) = Total SP − Gain = 153 − 63 = 90 units.

Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (63 ÷ 90) × 100 = 70%.

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of chairs sold = 153

Gain = Selling price of 63 chairs

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP − Gain

Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 CP = 90 Units
 Gain = 63 Units
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Total SP = 153 Units
 Profit % = (63 ÷ 90) × 100 = 70%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price (SP) of 1 chair be ₹1.

⇒ Total Selling Price of 153 chairs = ₹153.

⇒ Gain obtained = Selling Price of 63 chairs = ₹63.

⇒ Cost Price (CP) of 153 chairs = Total SP − Gain

⇒ CP = 153 − 63 = ₹90.

⇒ Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (63 ÷ 90) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (7 ÷ 10) × 100 = 70%.

**∴ The correct answer is 70%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss on Selling Price

If the loss incurred is equal to the selling price of 'x' units out of 'y' units sold, then the total Cost Price becomes (y + x) units. Loss % = x ÷ (y + x) × 100.

Profit or Loss on Cost Price

If the profit or loss is equal to the cost price of 'x' units out of 'y' units sold, then the Cost Price remains 'y' units. Profit/Loss % = x ÷ y × 100.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods claiming it is at cost price but uses a false lighter weight, the true cost incurred is for the false weight given. Profit % = (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.

questions.question: The salary of an employee is increased by 30%. By what percentage should the new salary be reduced in order to restore the original salary? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Required decrease % = [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%

Here, R = 30%

Required % = [30 ÷ (100 + 30)] × 100% = (30 ÷ 130) × 100%

Required % = 300 ÷ 13 ≈ 23.08%

**∴ The correct answer is 23.08%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial increase in salary = 30%

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Decrease = (Decrease ÷ New Value) × 100%

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Original
 100
 
 New
 130
 
 

 + 30%

 

 − ? %

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the original salary be 100.

⇒ Increased salary = 100 + (30% of 100) = 130

⇒ To restore the salary to 100, the new salary must be decreased by: 130 − 100 = 30

⇒ Required percentage decrease = (30 ÷ 130) × 100%

⇒ Required percentage decrease = 300 ÷ 13 %

⇒ Required percentage decrease = 23.0769... %

⇒ Required percentage decrease ≈ 23.08%

**∴ The correct answer is 23.08%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

The formula for finding the percentage change is [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100%. The calculation is always based strictly on the original value from which the change occurs.

Reversing a Percentage Increase

If a quantity is increased by x%, it must be decreased by [x ÷ (100 + x)] × 100% in order to return to its original value.

Successive Percentage Change

If a given value undergoes two successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change can be calculated directly using the formula: Net Change = (a + b + ab ÷ 100)%.
</p

questions.question: A, B and C can do a piece of work in 15 days, 30 days and 40 days, respectively. A starts working on the first day, A and B works on the second day and A and C works on the third day. This pattern is repeated till the work gets completed. In how many days will the work be over?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(15, 30, 40) = 120 units. Efficiencies: A = 8, B = 4, C = 3.

Work in 1 cycle of 3 days (A, A+B, A+C) = 8 + 12 + 11 = 31 units.

Work in 3 cycles (9 days) = 31 × 3 = 93 units. Remaining work = 120 − 93 = 27 units.

Day 10 (A): 8 units, Remaining = 19. Day 11 (A+B): 12 units, Remaining = 7.

Day 12 (A+C) time needed = 7/11 days. Total time = 11 + 7/11 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 11⁷/₁₁ days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 15 days

Time taken by B = 30 days

Time taken by C = 40 days

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A
 15
 120
 8
 
 

 B
 30
 4
 
 

 C
 40
 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done on 1st day by A = 8 units

⇒ Work done on 2nd day by A and B = 8 + 4 = 12 units

⇒ Work done on 3rd day by A and C = 8 + 3 = 11 units

⇒ Total work completed in 3 days (1 complete cycle) = 8 + 12 + 11 = 31 units

⇒ Number of full cycles possible = 120 ÷ 31 = 3 cycles

⇒ Work completed in 9 days (3 cycles) = 31 × 3 = 93 units

⇒ Remaining work = 120 − 93 = 27 units

⇒ Work done on 10th day by A = 8 units

⇒ Remaining work = 27 − 8 = 19 units

⇒ Work done on 11th day by A and B = 12 units

⇒ Remaining work = 19 − 12 = 7 units

⇒ The turn on the 12th day is of A and C with a combined efficiency of 11 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by A and C to complete the remaining 7 units = 7 ÷ 11 days

⇒ Total time taken = 9 + 1 + 1 + 7/11 = 11⁷/₁₁ days

**∴ The correct answer is 11⁷/₁₁ days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

When workers work on alternate days, find the combined work of one complete cycle (e.g., 2 or 3 days). Multiply the cycle to get as close to the total work as possible without exceeding it, then calculate the remaining work for the sequence step-by-step.

Work and Efficiency

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. If the time ratio of A and B is x:y, their efficiency ratio will be y:x. The fundamental formula used is: Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

Pipes and Cisterns

The core concept is identical to Time and Work. Inlets are treated as positive work (filling the tank), while outlets or leaks are treated as negative work (emptying the tank).
</p

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Selling Price is also calculated from Marked Price (MP) using the rule: SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Loss Percentage Formula

When an article is sold at a loss, the Selling Price becomes: SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Successive Profit

If an article passes through two sellers making profits P₁% and P₂%, the final SP = CP × (1 + P₁/100) × (1 + P₂/100).

questions.question: The force acting on an object is directly proportional to its mass. If a force of 10 N is required to move an object of mass 2 kg, what force (in newtons) is needed to move an object of mass 5 kg?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For directly proportional quantities, the multiplying factor remains constant.

Mass multiplier = 5 kg ÷ 2 kg = 2.5

Required force = Initial force × Mass multiplier

Required force = 10 × 2.5 = 25 N

**∴ The correct answer is 25 N.**

questions.question: Two trains having lengths of 450 m and 350 m are running at speeds of 80 km/h and 110 km/h, respectively, in the same direction. The time taken (in minutes) by the faster train, coming from behind, to completely cross the other train is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 110 − 80 = 30 km/h = 30 × (5/18) = 25/3 m/s.

Total distance to cross = 450 + 350 = 800 m.

Time = Total distance ÷ Relative speed = 800 ÷ (25/3) = 96 seconds.

Time in minutes = 96 ÷ 60 = 1.6 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of slower train (L₁) = 450 m

Length of faster train (L₂) = 350 m

Speed of slower train (V₁) = 80 km/h

Speed of faster train (V₂) = 110 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (same direction) = V₂ − V₁

Speed in m/s = Speed in km/h × (5/18)

Time taken = Total length ÷ Relative speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 110 − 80 = 30 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 30 × (5/18) = 150/18 = 25/3 m/s

⇒ Total distance to be covered = L₁ + L₂ = 450 + 350 = 800 m

⇒ Time taken = 800 ÷ (25/3)

⇒ Time taken = (800 × 3) ÷ 25 = 2400 ÷ 25 = 96 seconds

⇒ Time taken in minutes = 96 ÷ 60 = 1.6 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 1.6 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (V₂ − V₁).

Trains Moving in Opposite Directions

If two trains are moving in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (V₁ + V₂).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Rakesh invests a sum of ₹5400 and Shivam invests a sum of ₹10200 at the same rate of simple interest per annum. If, at the end of 4 years, Shivam gets ₹480 more interest than Rakesh, then find the rate of interest per annum (in percentage).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in Principal = ₹10200 − ₹5400 = ₹4800.

Difference in Simple Interest for 4 years = ₹480.

Difference in Interest per year = 480 ÷ 4 = ₹120.

Rate% = (Interest per year ÷ Difference in Principal) × 100

Rate% = (120 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rakesh's principal (P₁) = ₹5400

Shivam's principal (P₂) = ₹10200

Time (T) = 4 years

Difference in Simple Interest (SI₂ − SI₁) = ₹480

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 Rakesh: ₹5400
 Interest = I

 
 Shivam: ₹10200
 Interest = I + 480
 
 

 

 
 Difference: ₹4800
 Interest Diff: ₹480 (4 Yrs)
 Diff/Yr = ₹120
 
 Rate = (120 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 2.5%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Difference in SI = [(P₂ × R × T) ÷ 100] − [(P₁ × R × T) ÷ 100]

⇒ 480 = [(10200 × R × 4) ÷ 100] − [(5400 × R × 4) ÷ 100]

⇒ 480 = 408R − 216R

⇒ 480 = 192R

⇒ R = 480 ÷ 192

⇒ R = 2.5

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Difference Rule

The difference in simple interest for two different principals over the same time and rate is calculated directly using the difference in their principal amounts: SI Difference = (Principal Difference × Rate × Time) ÷ 100.

Simple vs Compound Interest

In Simple Interest, interest is calculated only on the principal amount for the entire period. In Compound Interest, interest is calculated on both principal and accumulated interest leading to an exponential curve.

Constant Rate Property

If time and rate are constant, the Simple Interest earned is directly proportional to the Principal invested. Thus, SI₁ ÷ P₁ = SI₂ ÷ P₂.

questions.question: Veer has ₹1632 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Nitin and Pravin and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Nitin and Pravin got same amount after 12 and 13 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Veer give to Nitin?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal in Compound Interest, the ratio of principals is given by (1 + R/100)t² − t¹.

Ratio of Nitin's share to Pravin's share = (1 + 4/100)¹³ − ¹² = 104/100 = 26/25.

Total ratio parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts.

Nitin's share = (26 / 51) × 1632 = 26 × 32 = 832.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹832.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Total money = ₹1632

Rate of interest (R) = 4% compounded annually

Time for Nitin (n₁) = 12 years

Time for Pravin (n₂) = 13 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ
